Financial figures are from the FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0001628280-26-003942, filed January 29, 2026); ownership is from the 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001628280-26-025532, filed April 16, 2026, record date April 1, 2026). OWNERSHIP: the proxy gives Zuckerberg 639,347 Class A shares (marked * for less than 1% of Class A), 341,823,978 Class B shares (99.8% of Class B) and 60.8% of total voting power, but no percentage of all shares, so pctEconomic is null and the 13.49% economic share is in leader.derived (both class counts quoted). Footnote (2): the Class A shares are held by Chan Zuckerberg Biohub, Inc., over which he has sole voting and investment power 'but no pecuniary interest'; the Class B shares are held by the Mark Zuckerberg Trust (3,388,097), CZI Holdings, LLC (109,373,980), Chan Zuckerberg Holdings, LLC (17,061,801), CZI Holdings I, LLC (12,000,000, pledged as collateral for indebtedness), Chan Zuckerberg Holdings II, III, IV and V, LLC (50,000,000 each) and CZ Management, LLC (100). No options or RSUs are included. 5% HOLDERS: the proxy lists only BlackRock (7.2%) and FMR (6.1%), as % of Class A only, and those are the figures recorded; on an all-shares basis they would be lower (Class B is about 13.5% of all shares), and they are not recomputed. Their total-voting-power percentages are 2.8% and 2.4%. Both rest on old Schedule 13G/A filings (BlackRock February 12, 2024), so holder asOf is omitted. Vanguard, listed at 8.5% of Class A in the 2025 proxy, is gone: footnote (21) says its Schedule 13G/A of March 27, 2026 reported no beneficial ownership after an internal realignment on January 12, 2026 under which its subsidiaries report separately, and none of them had filed by the proxy date. CASH: buybacks are cash paid for Class A repurchases in 2025 ($26,248m). Dividends include dividend equivalents on RSUs. GEOGRAPHY: Europe includes Russia and Turkey; Rest of World includes Africa, Latin America and the Middle East (10-K footnote 2); United States alone was $74.78 billion (footnote 1). No employee stock purchase plan appears in the 10-K, so plan is null.

studies.title: Meta's Economic Contribution in the U.S. (2024)

ecosystem.notes: The FY2025 10-K has no flow measure, so measure is null. The study is still Meta's own 2024 U.S. estimate: the study page, rechecked November 24, 2026, still reports 2024 figures, and no newer edition was found, so it is kept. It was announced May 13, 2025 ("a new study we conducted") and covers the U.S. only. It starts from Meta's estimate that each U.S. ad dollar yields $3.71 of advertiser revenue ("over $215 billion in business/advertisers revenues in the U.S. from Meta ads"), then applies BEA input-output multipliers for indirect and induced activity, so the $548 billion is a modelled economic-activity figure, not money paid to businesses or creators. It includes about $2 billion of Meta's own non-advertising sales. The study year (2024) is a year earlier than the platform revenue (FY2025), and Meta revenue is worldwide, so the two are not comparable.

linkedOutput.label: Economic output linked to Meta's advertising technologies
linkedOutput.definition: Meta's own estimate: 'Meta's advertising technologies are linked to $X billion in gross economic output annually.' Based on experimental research (Meta's 2024 US advertising revenue of $58 billion led to $215 billion in advertiser revenue across all states); total output for linked supply chains is estimated with BEA input-output tables. A modelled estimate of activity at advertisers and their supply chains, not Meta's own spending.

linkedJobs.label: Jobs linked to Meta's advertising technologies
linkedJobs.definition: Meta's own estimate of employment in advertisers' supply chains linked to its advertising technologies, from the same BEA input-output model. These are not Meta employees.

activeBusinesses.label: Businesses actively using Facebook
activeBusinesses.definition: Meta's estimate of businesses in the state that actively use Facebook; 'Active businesses are defined as those with a Facebook Page that has been logged into within the past month.'

footprint.notes: usStates: one row per state from Meta's own 'Meta in <State>' fact sheets (research.facebook.com/economiccontribution, 50 states; no DC sheet), each read in full. They carry 2024 data (published 2025); no newer edition found (checked 2026-11-24: the economiccontribution page still gives the 2024 national figures, $548 billion and 3.4 million jobs). Output and jobs are Meta's modelled estimates of activity at advertisers and their supply chains linked to Meta ads (BEA input-output multipliers), not Meta payroll or spending. research.facebook.com refuses scripted requests, so the 50 PDFs were opened in a real browser (each redirects to a signed fbcdn.net copy, downloaded and read); source.url is the stable research.facebook.com/file/... address, which the automated quote checker cannot fetch. Long-lived assets are from the FY2025 10-K, which discloses only the U.S. and the rest of the world (no other country above 10%). Sites: corporate HQ from the FY2025 10-K (about 10 million square feet, including about two million unoccupied; the 10-K says Meta owns 30 data center locations globally), plus data centers from datacenters.atmeta.com (re-read 2026-11-24, undated; all 11 quoted entries unchanged). Selection rule, kept from the last edition: every data center outside North America, and the seven U.S. data centers with the largest stated investment among sites that broke ground in 2024 or earlier. Sites listed as breaking ground in 2025 or later (El Paso TX, $10 billion+, and Bowling Green OH and Beaver Dam WI, 2025; Lebanon IN, $10 billion+, Tulsa OK and Sturgeon County AB, 2026) are left out to stay within 12. Several states host more than one data center (AL, IN, OH, TX), so data-center figures are not summed into states. Revenue by geography is in the records and not repeated.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 10-K, accession 0001628280-26-003942). Capex is purchases of property and equipment only; intangibles are combined with business acquisitions in one line (4,231 in 2025) and left out. Principal payments on finance leases (2,524) are in financing activities and are not added.

pay.notes: Employees: year-end count from the FY2025 10-K. Payroll: the 10-K gives no total of salaries, benefits or personnel costs (it describes headcount-related costs only as parts of each expense line), so the 2026 proxy's CEO pay ratio median for 2025 is used. Meta identified its median employee using total direct compensation (salary, bonus or commission and the value of equity awards granted in 2025), with the employee population determined at October 31, 2025; the CEO pay ratio is 65:1.
